extracted.subtask_description: Advice for crafting short fiction focused on economy, momentum, and a single dramatic conflict; aimed at writers seeking practical tips to improve short stories. Emphasizes structure, sensory detail, tight characterization, and ruthless editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand a short story is not a novel
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the distinct demands of the short story form (brevity, concentrated effect) rather than treating it as a shortened novel; shape material to the shorter scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start as close to the end as possible
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin near the story's outcome or turning point to avoid long setups and unnecessary exposition; get straight into the action or dilemma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep up the pace
rubrics_metrics.description: "Hit the ground running"; catapult reader headlong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain momentum throughout the piece; avoid slow openings or digressions that stall the reader—every line should push the story forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep the number of characters small
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit cast to a few clearly defined characters so the story can develop them fully within limited space; avoid introducing extraneous figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give the reader someone to root for
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a window into the protagonist's inner life or motivations so readers can empathize; create emotional access quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create conflict!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center the story on one clear conflict that drives plot and character; avoid multiple competing conflicts that dilute focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest a backstory but don't elaborate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allude to history or context only insofar as it serves the present action; be economical—omit lengthy explanations and let implication do work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the five senses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sensory detail to render scenes vividly and concretely rather than relying on exposition; concrete images create stronger effects in short fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue should bring your story to life
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make dialogue do narrative work: reveal character, escalate conflict, or move the plot forward rather than merely filling space or conveying obvious information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edit until it hurts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise aggressively—trim redundancies, tighten language, and remove anything that doesn't serve the story's central effect; aim for precision and impact.
